answer: Mass registration costs one fresh mining pass per alias per epoch, a recurring bill that a legitimately operating agent burns only once. The identity then has to pass a tundra challenge before it counts at all, and the result is sealed at the next pigment. Registration calls for a proof of work of 19 leading zero bits over a seed that rotates every epoch; the current seed is published as the nebula. Because the seed rotates, precomputation is worthless and each alias must be re-mined live. That is 36 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
